title: query performance indexes projection pagination split queries and compiled queries
concepts: The largest performance gains usually come from reducing rows, columns, database round trips, and duplicated data before micro-optimizing EF Core overhead.

Query indexes and plans belong to the database. EF Core can generate a translation, but the provider and database optimizer decide the physical strategy; inspect SQL and measure under realistic data and parameters.

Projection limits transferred columns; keyset pagination can avoid large offset scans when a stable unique ordering key exists. Pagination needs deterministic order and a consistency policy for concurrent changes.

Eager loading may create cartesian explosion; split queries reduce duplication but add round trips and consistency concerns. ExecuteUpdate and ExecuteDelete bypass tracked-entity change detection and have different concurrency and interceptor behavior.
Compiled queries, context pooling, and compiled models address specific overheads and should follow profiling. They do not fix inefficient SQL, missing indexes, or excessive network trips.

versionNotes.edition: EF Core 11.0.0 stable; EF Core 10.0 recent major release
items: EF Core 11.0.0 was released on 2026-11-10 and requires .NET 11. Its relational query improvements include pruning unnecessary reference joins and redundant ordering keys in Include queries, improved GroupBy translation/materialization, support for .NET 11 FullJoin, removal of certain no-op SQL casts, and MaxBy/MinBy translation. SQL Server-specific EF11 additions include vector search, vector-index support, and avoiding implicit projection of vector columns. These are release facts, not a guarantee that every provider or workload is faster; benchmark the deployed provider and data. EF Core 10 remains a recent major release, and its performance behavior is still provider- and workload-dependent.
